clue.text: Reimagined — once fog clears — same crime of 14/20

indicators.note: something reimagined is pictured afresh in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weather report: the scene looks different once the fog lifts, revealing the same old crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once fog clears' reads like a time phrase but is part of the anagram fodder along with 'same'. 14/20 is the Master of Stair, John Dalrymple, who ordered the 1692 killing of the MacDonalds in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1692 slaughter of MacDonalds in a Highland glen was ordered by Dalrymple, so it is the atrocity laid at his door.

clue.text: I want to rise in sober society — vigour lacks in it

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the letters of the sober society

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a society for staying sober

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the words I and want are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to want to do something is to mean to do it

explanation.surface: A recovering drinker wishes to climb in the temperance group, though lacking the energy for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition marked by too few red blood cells, leaving the sufferer pale, tired and without energy.

clue.text: Few protecting millions in war zone

indicators.note: the word for few wraps around the other letter as if guarding it

parts.note: a few means some
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A small band guards millions of people caught in a combat area.
explanation.definitionFit: The French river was the scene of a huge First World War battle in 1916, a byword for a deadly battlefield.

clue.text: Man, classically elegant, refuses cold food

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: the word for classically elegant turns away one of its letters

parts.note: Attic describes the refined style of ancient Athens
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A refined gentleman of classical tastes turns down a chilly dish.
explanation.definitionFit: An unleavened Indian flatbread, an example of something eaten.

clue.text: ETA presses ten Fairy Fellows into explosive testing

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters have other pieces pushed into them
an explosion scatters things, so the letters of ETA and into are blown into a new order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
a peri is a fairy in Persian myth
fellows are men

explanation.surface: The Basque separatist group ETA presses ten fairy people into bomb testing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive' scrambles ETA and 'into' into ETATION, and 'presses' pushes XPERIMEN into it after the first E. ETA was an armed Basque separatist group, which suits the bomb surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying out trials or tests to find something out is the scientific sense of the word.

clue.text: US poet over years lacking enthusiasm

indicators.note: in a down clue the poet's name sits above the next letter

parts.note: Robert Frost was an American poet

explanation.surface: An American poet, getting on in years, has lost his zest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold, unfriendly manner is a chilly reception, showing no warmth or eagerness.

clue.text: Old man flees injured wizard

indicators.note: the father's letters run away from the word for injured

parts.note: injured means damaged
old man is slang for father, dad

explanation.surface: A father runs away from a wounded sorcerer.
explanation.walkthrough: D, A and the final D of DAMAGED leave, scattered, in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician or learned sorcerer, a literary word for a wizard.

clue.text: Rainwear put on shivery lad clan caught in 1/8

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat
to don clothes is to put them on

indicators.note: shivering shakes things, so the letters of lad are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cold boy dons a raincoat, his clan trapped in a Highland glen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish clan whose members were slaughtered by government troops in that glen in 1692.

clue.text: See 1
Old 7 down had this fine weapon

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: An old clansman possessed this splendid weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old 7 down' gives OLD MACDONALD, the nursery rhyme farmer: 'Old MacDonald had a farm'.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme says the old farmer owned this agricultural holding with its animals.

clue.text: Brave daughter giving sportsman hug made advances

indicators.note: the outer letters wrap round the sportsman as in an embrace

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, such as an Apache
a pro is a professional sportsman

explanation.surface: A courageous girl gives an athlete a cuddle and makes a move on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun: a Native American warrior, here an Apache.
explanation.definitionFit: To come nearer, or to make overtures to someone, is to make advances.

clue.text: Brainless life-form a second President recalled?

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: called back, so the president's name is read backwards

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president

explanation.surface: A quip that some president, briefly remembered, was a mindless creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-celled organism, which has no nervous system at all.

clue.text: Upset Carter to reference past events

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An unsettled President Carter refers back to history.
explanation.definitionFit: To act backwards in time, applying to or bearing on matters already past.

clue.text: Flexible assistant's uppermost part almost against belly

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: the face is the top or exposed surface of something
to can mean against, as in cheek to cheek
tum is informal for stomach, belly

explanation.surface: A supple helper's top half is almost pressed against their stomach, like a contortionist.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant or employee who does all kinds of jobs, from Latin for 'do everything'.

clue.text: John Dalrymple: flight controller?

definitions.meaning: the Scottish Secretary of State behind the 1692 massacre, known by his title
jokingly, one who controls a flight of steps

explanation.surface: A historical figure is described as if he were an air traffic controller.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalrymple held the Scottish title of Stair; a flight of stairs is what such a lord would command.

clue.text: Conservative on the beer — smart man?

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A Tory on the booze: is he a clever fellow?
explanation.definitionFit: A smart Alec is a know-it-all, so this name is the one the phrase pins on the clever man.

clue.text: One tested bomb aboard chopper going north and east

indicators.note: the bomb is carried inside the other letters like cargo
in a down clue going north means the word for chopper is read upwards

parts.note: an axe is a chopper
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: A device is tested by putting a bomb on a helicopter flying north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' suggests a helicopter but means an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate sitting a test is a person being tested.

clue.text: Overly sentimental sports supporter keeps wicket

indicators.note: the supporter holds the wicket letter inside it

parts.note: a tee supports the ball in golf
W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A mawkish fan holds on to a cricket wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports supporter' suggests a fan but is a golf tee, the peg the ball rests on.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively dainty, cute or quaint; a British informal word for sugary sweetness.

clue.text: King shows purpose early in the morning

parts.note: will means determination or purpose
1 am, read as I AM, is an early hour

explanation.surface: A monarch shows his resolve before dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Several English kings bore this name, including the Conqueror.

clue.text: One departs north exit closer in adjacent house

indicators.note: the letter for one leaves the word for exit

parts.note: taken as written before its letter goes
I is the Roman numeral for one
a door is what closes a room off

explanation.surface: Someone leaves by the north exit, closer to the neighbouring house.
explanation.definitionFit: Living in the neighbouring home is living beside you.

clue.text: See 14
Stops before finishing topside of beef in spoilt roast

indicators.note: the first letter of beef goes inside the jumbled roast
a spoilt roast is ruined, so its letters are messed up
the top of a down entry is its first letter

explanation.surface: The cook halts mid-dinner because the topside of beef in the roast is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topside' is a real cut of beef, which disguises the first-letter signal; 'spoilt' rearranges ROAST to AORTS round B.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a mission or process before completion is to call it off partway.

clue.text: Palace where an innocent artist captures hearts

parts.note: the article an gives A

indicators.note: the outer letters seize the hearts letter and hold it

parts.note: a lamb is a byword for an innocent
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A naive painter wins hearts in a royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moorish fortress-palace in Granada, Spain.

clue.text: Small Sea States for jellyfish

parts.note: the Med is the short form of the Mediterranean Sea
the USA is the United States

explanation.surface: A list of seas and nations to look up for a marine creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The free-swimming bell-shaped stage of a jellyfish is the zoological term borrowed from the snake-haired Gorgon.

clue.text: See nothing in small room in Tavistock Place?

indicators.note: the first in puts the letters for see and nothing inside the small room

parts.note: a den is a small private room
V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Look at an empty den in a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: Tavistock Place is a London street, but here it is the Devon market town of Tavistock, and its county is the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The English West Country county where the market town of Tavistock lies.

clue.text: Sort idiot out with new twist on meaning?

indicators.note: out means not in proper order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Straighten out a fool who keeps putting a new spin on what words mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Misrepresenting what was said gives a skewed, warped version of its sense.

clue.text: Some dive a little lower for food?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Dip slightly lower to find something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' looks like 'more low' but is one that lows: a calf, eaten as meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Calf meat; a lower is a cow or calf that moos, here served as a meal.

clue.text: Song about masculine Arabic man?

indicators.note: the song goes round the masculine letter

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A song about a manly figure from Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim commander or ruler, the title of a prince in the Arab world.

clue.text: Sick room, fit medic and oxygen in Californian city

parts.note: a san is a sanatorium, a sickroom in a school
lean means slim and fit
Dr is a doctor
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A sickroom, a healthy doctor and an oxygen supply in a West Coast town.
explanation.definitionFit: A city on the eastern shore of San Francisco Bay in the US state of California.
